title: Company trajectory resilience playbook
summary: Working playbook for a 6–12 week course-correction and comms plan designed to protect company trajectory during demand shocks, hiring adjustments, or product delivery slippage. Combines proposed OKR pivots, an executive update template, and an all-hands run-of-show with contingency scripts.
purpose: Give execs and program leads a single, actionable artifact to run a trajectory resilience week: decide OKR trims, align comms, rehearse all-hands narratives, and create a short-term resourcing plan.
objectives: Reduce uncertainty: surface three discrete scenarios with measurable triggers
Preserve momentum: select a minimal set of OKR commitments to defend core KPIs
Communicate clearly: unified exec script + FAQ for engineering and GTM
Define 30/60/90 operational steps and owners for escalation and rollback
recommended_okr_adjustments: Tier OKRs into defend / defer / decompress buckets. Defend = must-deliver KPIs tied to customer SLAs and revenue; defer = high-impact but non-critical projects; decompress = nice-to-have experimental work.
For each team, list one defended OKR, one deferred OKR, and one decompression candidate. This creates cross-team clarity for prioritization conversations.
Example: Product-hosted-api: defend = 99.9% p95 latency across top-3 routes; defer = new analytics dashboard milestone; decompress = experimental model-quantization research spike.
scenarios_and_triggers: Scenario A — Mild headwind: 5–10% slower adoption vs plan. Trigger: 2 consecutive weeks of <90% forecasted signups. Action: pause non-defend hiring, accelerate small product fixes, maintain PS cadence.

Scenario B — Moderate disruption: 10–25% revenue deviation or 2 critical infra incidents in 30 days. Trigger: revenue < 75% projection or incident SLO breaches. Action: institute hiring slowdown, freeze non-core releases, prioritize Dedicated customer SLAs, prepare external comms draft.

Scenario C — Severe shock: >25% revenue decline or regulatory blocking issue. Trigger: multi-week revenue shortfall or compliance escalation. Action: immediate cross-functional exec war-room, targeted cost reduction plan, proactive customer outreach and SLA compensation planning.
allhands_run_of_show: Duration: 60 minutes (45 min presentation + 15 min live Q&A)
Opening (5m): CEO framing — state where we are, why we met, principle-level commitment to transparency.
State of the business (10m): CFO + Growth — high-level metrics, scenarios, and topline actions being considered.
Product & Roadmap (10m): Head of Product — what we will defend, what we will pause, and expected user impact.
Engineering & Reliability (8m): SRE lead — what we’re doing to maintain SLAs and incident posture.
People & Hiring (5m): People Ops — hiring pauses, internal transfers, compensation signals.
Support & CS (5m): CS lead — how customers are being prioritized and supported.
Commitments (2m): Ops lead — 7 concrete commitments we will deliver in 30 days and owners.
Q&A (15m): live, with pre-collected questions highlighted; fallback answers for sensitive topics.
Close (1m): CEO — reiterate trust, next sync cadence, where to find details.
exec_update_template: One-pager summary (top 3 bullets): current state, top decision needed, recommended executive ask.
Metrics snapshot: 3 leading + 3 lagging metrics with trend lines and variance from plan.
Risks & Mitigations: ordered list of top 5 risks with immediate mitigation steps and owners.
Decisions requested: clear yes/no choices with impact statements (e.g., pause hiring for X vs. reduce contractor spend by Y).
Communication ask: recommended staff message, external customer note, and comms owner.
communication_playbook: Day 0 (exec decision): internal exec memo + leadership briefing deck. Keep messaging aligned with scenario chosen.
Day 1 (all-hands): transparent townline + FAQ published to #all and Confluence page. Encourage managers to host skip-levels.
Day 2–7: team-level syncs to translate defend/defer guidance into team plans. Product/Eng should publish a short action list.
Customer comms: prioritized outreach to top 20 accounts (if revenue-related) with assigned AE/CS owner. Template in linked_artifacts.
External: if public-facing impacts exist, draft customer-facing note and press line; legal reviews required.
decision_thresholds_and_owners: Hiring pause threshold: exec approval required if company cash runway < 9 months OR scenario B triggers. Owner: Head of People + CFO.
Release freeze threshold: if p95 latency > target for 48 hours or two P1 incidents in 7 days. Owner: Head of Engineering + SRE.
Customer SLA escalation: any Dedicated customer with SLA breach triggers immediate remediation and credit plan. Owner: CS Director + VP of Product.
Comm trigger: CEO approves external comms; Head of Comms drafts within 24 hours.
short_term_tactical_checklist: Assemble cross-functional war-room (ops, product, eng, finance, legal, comms) -> daily 30m for first 10 days.
Each lead submits a 1-page defend/ defer/ decompress plan within 48 hours.
Create a prioritized incident response runbook and reroute on-call rotations for high-risk components.
Freeze non-essential vendor spend > $10k/month pending review.
Prepare a manager FAQ and guidance kit for skip-level conversations.
open_questions: Should we adopt a company-level hiring pause threshold at 9 months runway or make it a rolling decision based on monthly cash flow?
How granular should defend/defer categorization be for cross-functional projects that touch multiple teams?
What cadence for executive check-ins is sustainable without creating meeting fatigue? (daily war-room -> semi-weekly exec review -> weekly all-hands?)
